[FACT] User recently had an amazing seafood paella in Barcelona during a week-long vacation with family.  
[FACT] User stayed in a lovely apartment in the Gothic Quarter of Barcelona.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking for authentic Spanish recipes or recommendations for seafood paella.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Barcelona's Gothic Quarter is a wonderful place to stay and offers delicious cuisine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Traditional Valencian-Style Seafood Paella Recipe includes ingredients such as 1 cup uncooked Spanish rice, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 onion, 2 cloves garlic, 1 pound shrimp, 1 pound mussels, 1 pound clams, 1 pound squid, 1 teaspoon saffron threads, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon salt, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, 2 cups fish stock, 1 cup water, and lemon wedges for serving.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Instructions for making paella include heating oil, cooking onion and garlic, adding seafood, and simmering rice with stock and water.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for paella include using a variety of seafood, adding chorizo, and achieving a crispy crust called "socarrat."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Other recommendations for paella include using lobster, crab, scallops, artichoke hearts, or roasted red peppers, and experimenting with spices like cumin or coriander.  
[PREFERENCE] User plans to try the traditional Valencian-style paella recipe first.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking for a good Spanish wine to pair with the paella.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended wines include Albariño, Verdejo, and Bobal for white wines, and Rosado and Tempranillo for rosé or red wines.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Specific wine recommendations include Bodega El Sequé, Albariño (around $20), Marqués de Riscal, Verdejo (around $15), Bodega Chozas Carrascal, Bobal (around $15), Bodegas Hispano Suizas, Rosado (around $12), and Finca Antigua, Tempranillo (around $10).  
[PREFERENCE] User has had Albariño before and loved its crispness.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] La Rambla is an iconic spot in Barcelona known for its energy and charm.
